investigations.name: s0-coupling-calibration
investigations.title: Coupling calibration (NF-kB switching speed and the death clock)
investigations.objective: How fast must the Boolean NF-kB node follow Lipniacki's nuclear NF-kB (kappa), and how fast is the death machinery (k_time), for the composite's survival / apoptosis / necrosis split under TNF to depend on NF-kB at all?
investigations.claim: Under TNF held on at saturation, the coupled composite kills nearly every cell. None is alive at 24 h at 2-30 min per Calzone unit for any kappa, and 6.5-16% at 120 min per unit. Calzone's own network also kills nearly every cell (survival 1.4%), but the coupling shifts that death toward necrosis. Protective products that never decay (Study 0c, an upper bound) leave 3%, 8.5% and 13% alive at 2, 10 and 30 min per unit, and 33.5% at 120 min per unit (grid 16%). Protein persistence is therefore a real lever, but the measured rate does not pull it: with Lipniacki's protein turnover rate on those products (Study 0d, the corrected 0b), 0, 0, 0 and 12% are alive, no alive/dead change beyond noise. At 2-30 min per unit nearly every cell dies before NF-kB settles, during its first wave and the damped oscillation after it. At 120 min per unit the measured turnover is faster than the grid's switch-off and removes the durable survivors.

investigations.name: s1-survival-validation
investigations.title: Survival under TNF (validation against NF-kB-dependent survival)
investigations.objective: Under held, saturating TNF, can the composite let most cells with working NF-kB survive, while cells without NF-kB still die, using only the published models' own parameters? If not, where is the limit?
investigations.claim: Under held, saturating TNF the composite does not meet the standard, read as held survival, at any death clock: NF-kB's net protection is at most about 10-13 points at 24 h, and where most intact cells are alive (200 min per unit and slower) it is because many have not yet reached any fate. The limit is Calzone's own race between caspase-8 and NF-kB's activation route, both on the death clock; the coupling lowers protection further only at fast and middle clocks.
